subject: Urgent: Medirect production throttling — burst/quota config mismatch
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena@medirect.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: support@medirect.com, stephanie@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 19 Oct 2025 23:12:00 -0000
Subject: Production alerts: repeated 429s and high latency since 22:40 UTC

Hi Vivek / Marissa —

We started seeing a spike in 429 responses and token-level latency around 22:40 UTC tonight. Traffic pattern looks normal on our side; concurrent sessions and request rates unchanged. Our user-facing predictions are degrading (timeouts and retries).

We're attaching a short CSV of sample request IDs and timestamps. Can you confirm whether there's a known quota change or new burst policy rolling out? We're on the dedicated pool (DED-13) and saw a sharp drop in throughput to ~6 rps from normal ~120 rps.

Attachments: request_logs_2025-10-19.csv

This is customer-impacting — please escalate if you need exec attention.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ramos
Lead SRE, Medirect Health
elena@medirect.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor@redwood.com>, Elena Ramos <elena@medirect.com>, support@medirect.com
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 00:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Production alerts: repeated 429s and high latency since 22:40 UTC

Thanks for the heads-up, Elena — I'm on it.

Initial read from the logs Elena shared: we see a policy enforcement spike from the rategateway service that started right at 22:39:51 UTC. The policy snapshot attached (policy_snapshot_20251019.json) shows a new burst window rule with a very aggressive per-tenant burst cap (10 tokens / 30s) that looks like it was applied to the DED-13 tenant yesterday as part of an automated safety valve rollout.

Immediate next steps I am running now:
- Ask infra to pause the safety-valve rollout for DED pools (Connor)
- Roll back the burst cap on DED-13 to the previous profile (Marissa / Runtime)
- Apply temporary rate-exemptions for Medirect for the next 2 hours so customer traffic stabilizes

Marissa / Stephanie — can you confirm who owns the rollout and whether a canary gating failure triggered the wider application? If we can't rollback in <30m we should elevate to ops on-call and prepare an exec note for Legal/Customer Execs.

V

--
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor@redwood.com>, Elena Ramos <elena@medirect.com>, support@medirect.com
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 00:28:12 -0000
Subject: Re: Production alerts: repeated 429s and high latency since 22:40 UTC

On Sun, 19 Oct 2025 23:12:00 -0000 Elena Ramos wrote:
> We started seeing a spike in 429 responses and token-level latency around 22:40 UTC tonight.

Agree with Vivek's assessment — the burst/quota rule was pushed as part of a staged safety policy change that was intended to limit runaway cost for a subset of bursty tenants. Canary was green on small dev tenants but the gating condition missed a target metric (sequence length distribution) and it incorrectly matched DED-13.

Quick mitigation implemented (00:22 UTC):
- Pause automated rollout (Connor confirmed)
- Reapply previous burst caps for DED-13 (in progress)
- Created a temporary route override to bypass the burst enforcement for Medirect until 02:30 UTC

I have asked Runtime (kuan/runtime) to confirm the rollback completes and to validate KV cache warmup — we saw increased cold-kv misses which compounded latency.

Attachments: policy_snapshot_20251019.json

Marissa
Director, Runtime Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ramos <elena@medirect.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: support@medirect.com
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 02:01:40 -0000
Subject: Re: Production alerts: repeated 429s and high latency since 22:40 UTC

Thanks — traffic is recovering after the override. Latency back to acceptable levels (p90 down from 1.8s to 260ms) and 429s have stopped.

Two asks from Medirect:
1) Can Redwood provide a short post-mortem describing the gating failure and the policy change timeline (who approved the rule, why the canary did not catch this)?
2) We need a temporary SLA credit for the 1.5 hours of degraded availability. Please advise next steps.

I've attached a screenshot of the client errors during the window (screenshot_429_1019.png).

Best,
Elena
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ramos <elena@medirect.com>, support@medirect.com
Date: Mon, 20 Oct 2025 15:42:00 -0000
Subject: Executive summary + proposed remediation and asks for approval

Team — final update for exec thread:

Summary:
- Incident: Medirect production experienced request throttling (429s) and elevated token latency from 22:39–00:21 UTC due to an overly restrictive burst cap that matched DED-13.
- Root cause: A staged safety-valve policy intended to limit burst credit consumption was released with a gating rule that used an incorrect sequence-length predicate. Canary checks passed for control tenants but did not simulate DED-13's long-tail request shapes. Policy applied to DED-13 and reduced effective throughput. Cold KV misses amplified latency.

Impact:
- Customer-facing degradation for ~1.5 hours; peak error rate 18% 429s, p95 latency peaked at 2.1s. Potential SLA delta with Medirect; they have requested an SLA credit.

Actions taken (completed):
- Paused the safety-valve rollout across DED pools (Connor)
- Rolled back burst cap for DED-13 to prior profile (Marissa)
- Applied temporary route override to exempt Medirect while rollback completed
- Collected logs and created SUP ticket SUP-3712 for follow-up

Proposed next steps (ask for exec approval):
1) Approve a customer goodwill credit: propose 10% invoice credit for the impacted billing window (Legal/Finance sign-off needed).
2) Formal post-mortem to include: policy approval chain, canary gap analysis, and a plan to expand canary simulations (sequence-length, KV cold-warm scenarios).
3) Short-term control: add per-tenant soft-exemptions during policy rollouts and automatic rollback on >5% error rate within 15 minutes.
4) Longer-term: new rollout gating that includes synthetic traffic matching DED/enterprise tenants and a canary sweep for KV cache behavior.

Please reply with approvals or edits. If no objections in 60 minutes I will send a customer-facing post-mortem draft and coordinate the credit with Finance.

Vivek
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: request_logs_2025-10-19.csv, policy_snapshot_20251019.json, screenshot_429_1019.png
